question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I raised a replacement order with the backup supplier for the plant that makes Lacrivia. I did not record any allocation, because none of the affected packs meet the allocation rules. I also notified the five contracted accounts and handed the wholesaler notice to Trade Relations.

I followed the Supply Disruption Response process. No trusted playbook matched this situation, and the process rules covered everything I found, so I didn't search for unapproved playbooks.

## What I found
- **The late shipment:** S-103 (Castellan) has four open RM-103 (Glycerin USP) orders. The next one is PO000210: 3,300 units, promised for 2026-10-03, now expected around 2026-10-31. I assumed the three later orders (PO000211–213) are still on time.
- **Affected products:** RM-103 goes into five finished products:
  - At plant PL-01: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003).
  - At plant PL-02: Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001/2002).
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley) is qualified for RM-103 and active in the supplier portal. It is approved to ship **only to PL-01**. So Lacrivia and Cyclosporine OS are covered, but Oculon has no backup supplier.
- **DC stock (latest snapshot, 2026-09-25):**
  - Oculon is above safety stock at all three DCs, with about 27–39 days of supply.
  - Lacrivia is **already below safety stock at DC-EAST**: 46 units against 471 for 5 mL, and 34 against 233 for 10 mL. That is about 1–2 days of supply. The shortage was there before this delay; S-103's earlier orders all shipped on time.
- **When supply recovers at the DCs** (planned production times for each step):
  - Oculon: about 2026-12-16 (ship date plus 46 days), roughly 4 weeks later than planned.
  - Lacrivia: about late November, if S-111 ships in its usual ~23 days, plus 37 days.
- **Substitutes:** there is no approved company substitute. Cyclosporine OS also uses RM-103, so the same delay affects it (rule BR-SUB-01). Oculon has no approved substitute. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.

## Actions taken
| Step | Action | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Replacement order (SDR-2.2) | Purchase requisition to S-111: 3,300 units of RM-103 to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-10, marked expedite | **PR-9F89D38E** |
| Account teams (SDR-4.1) | One task per contracted account: no allocation, expected recovery, no substitute | Northfield **CRM-9986CC56**, Oak Hollow **CRM-0082FC3B**, Riverbend **CRM-469C9713**, Clearview **CRM-6360C80F**, Sunridge **CRM-C23FE0B4** |
| Wholesalers (SDR-4.2) | EDI has no API, so I opened a case for Trade Relations to notify W-01 through W-06 | **CASE-DED7F2B4** |
| Follow-ups | Case for the Supply Planning lead on the open Oculon and DC-EAST Lacrivia risks (see next section) | **CASE-18CC98AF** |

## What I did not do, and why
- **No allocation plans.** Under rule BR-ALLOC-02, a pack is allocated only if the delay cuts off its supply and it is below safety stock at a DC.
  - Lacrivia isn't allocated because S-111 can supply PL-01.
  - Oculon isn't allocated because it is above safety stock everywhere.
  - Because there was no plan, no approval request was needed.
- **No stock transfer to DC-EAST.** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold extra Lacrivia, but moving stock between DCs needs Supply Planning approval and isn't part of this process. I raised it in CASE-18CC98AF, together with:
  - getting S-111 approved to ship to PL-02 so Oculon has a backup;
  - confirming the later S-103 orders are on time;
  - checking how much RM-103 PL-02 has on hand.
- **No wholesaler inventory check.** That data feed isn't available until Q4 2026.

## Assumptions
- I ordered the full 3,300 units from S-111 for PL-01. The purchase order doesn't say which plant the units were for, and S-111 can only ship to PL-01.
- The need-by date is the original planned arrival (promised ship date plus 7 days in transit). S-111 will probably deliver later than that.
- "Contracted accounts" means the five health systems in the supply contracts list. Each buys through all three DCs, based on its clinics' last-13-week prescriptions.

**Knowledge-layer sources:** the Supply Disruption Response process (SDR-1.1 to 4.2), the supply trace, lead times for FG-1001 and FG-2001, and the reference sets supply_contracts and dc_service_regions. Rules applied: BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-APPR-01, BR-CUST-01 and BR-REGION-01. The days-of-supply figures use the governed days_of_supply metric.

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103' ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT DESC
SELECT SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, QUALIFIED_FLG, PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT PLANT_ID, MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','SEMI-060','CMP-320','RM-103') ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, PLANT_ID

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i JOIN (SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) MX FROM dbo.DC_INV GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID) m ON i.DC_ID=m.DC_ID AND i.MATERIAL_ID=m.MATERIAL_ID AND i.SNAPSHOT_DT=m.MX WHERE i.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SUM(UNITS) AS UNITS_28D, SUM(UNITS)/28.0 AS AVG_DAILY FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,(SELECT MAX(SHIP_DT) FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP)) GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
acct AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE, COALESCE(p2.ACCOUNT_ID, p1.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) AS TOP_ID
 FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p1 ON a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=p1.ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p2 ON p1.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=p2.ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT CASE WHEN ac.STATE IN ('IL','TX','MN','CO') THEN 'DC-CENTRAL' WHEN ac.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH') THEN 'DC-EAST' WHEN ac.STATE IN ('AZ','CA','WA') THEN 'DC-WEST' ELSE 'OTHER' END AS DC,
 r.PROD_NDC11, ac.TOP_ID, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) TRX13
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON r.PRSCRBR_ME=p.PRSCRBR_ME JOIN acct ac ON p.ACCOUNT_ID=ac.ACCOUNT_ID
WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110','99101030325','99101030350') AND ac.TOP_ID IN ('AC00117','AC00038','AC00059','AC00001','AC00138')
GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID, SUM(CASE WHEN s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-2001','FG-2002') THEN s.UNITS ELSE 0 END) OCULON_UNITS_28D, SUM(CASE WHEN s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') THEN s.UNITS ELSE 0 END) LACRIVIA_UNITS_28D FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,(SELECT MAX(SHIP_DT) FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP)) GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID ORDER BY s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID

escalation_cases.details:
SDR-4.2 handoff (wholesaler EDI gateway has no API). Please notify wholesalers W-01, W-02 (DC-EAST), W-03, W-04 (DC-CENTRAL), W-05, W-06 (DC-WEST).
Facts: S-103 will ship its next RM-103 (Glycerin USP) lot, PO000210 (3,300, promised 2026-10-03), ~4 weeks late (~2026-10-31). RM-103 feeds Lacrivia 5 mL (99101-0101-05) / 10 mL (99101-0101-10), Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL (99101-0202-05) and Oculon 2.5 mL (99101-0303-25) / 5 mL (99101-0303-50).
- Oculon (made at PL-02; no alternate supplier approved for PL-02): all DCs above safety stock today (~27-39 days of cover); replenishment from the delayed lot reaches DCs ~2026-12-16, about 4 weeks later than planned. Supply may tighten in November.
- Lacrivia / Cyclosporine OS (PL-01): resupplied from qualified alternate S-111 (PR-9F89D38E); material expected at DCs late Nov 2026. Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL already below safety stock at DC-EAST (46 and 34 units on hand on 2026-09-25), so W-01/W-02 Lacrivia orders may be short in the near term.
No allocation plan recorded (no affected pack qualifies under BR-ALLOC-02). No approved company substitute (BR-SUB-01/02).

escalation_cases.subject: RM-103 delay: follow-ups outside the response process – Oculon has no alternate at PL-02; Lacrivia below safety stock at DC-EAST
escalation_cases.details:
FYI and decision needed (not actioned by the agent):
1) Oculon (FG-2001/FG-2002, PL-02) relies only on S-103 for RM-103 at PL-02; alternate S-111 is qualified for RM-103 but approved in the supplier portal only for PL-01. Oculon DC stock is above safety stock now but has ~27-39 days of cover against recovery ~2026-12-16 (S-103 ship ~10-31 + 46-day lead time per get_lead_times). Consider: getting S-111 approved for PL-02 (Supplier Quality/Procurement), confirming with S-103 that later POs PO000211-213 stay on time, and checking PL-02 RM-103 on hand. If an Oculon pack falls below safety stock at a DC, rerun the response to allocate.
2) Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001) and 10 mL (FG-1002) are already below safety stock at DC-EAST (46/471 and 34/233 units, snapshot 2026-09-25; ~1-2 days of cover). This was not caused by the S-103 delay (its earlier POs shipped on time), and under BR-ALLOC-02 the packs are not allocated because S-111 covers PL-01 (PR-9F89D38E raised). DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold Lacrivia above safety stock (FG-1001 excess ~363 / ~332 units; FG-1002 ~196 / ~195). Any inter-DC transfer needs your approval (BR-ALLOC-01/BR-APPR-01). The agent did not propose a transfer.
